accepted_nonvisual_foundation: The approved ScrapDrum body is present, legible and unchanged in Flight hero, macro and gameplay captures.
The new item-scoped StrictCustomDerived prefab/material/body hierarchy remains the correct ownership boundary.
R3 is substantially less overblown than R2 and no longer contains the enormous blurry cones or thick fluorescent rod bundle.
visual_rejection_findings: Muzzle still reads as a raw bundle of long uniform white/red needles crossing a dominant white torus. It has no compact white-hot pressure core, no broad warm wedge and no authored opacity falloff.

Several muzzle streaks extend backward and laterally across the origin, so the +Z firing direction is visually ambiguous and the shape looks like editor debug lines rather than a commercial muzzle flash.

Flight hero and macro are almost entirely the body. The attached wake is reduced to isolated hairline needles at the rear, with no compact coherent pale/brass kinetic plume or visible particulate transition.
Impact repeats nearly the same torus-and-line construction as Muzzle instead of forming a distinct contact core, broken fan, tapered spark burst and expanding residue.
Impact decay is nearly black and unreadable at the review exposure, so it does not prove a controlled short residue phase.
The baseline comparison makes the gap explicit: the new M/F/I are thinner, more uniform and less volumetric than Gunner_Bullet and the supplied school-quality references.
Clean hierarchy and 30-cycle residue metrics cannot substitute for the failed visual gate.
required_r4_rebuild: Freeze R3 evidence and keep the approved body/FBX/material remaps/hierarchy unchanged. Rebuild only the new derived VFX recipes and new derived VFX textures/materials.

Stop using long stretched-billboard needles as the primary language. Create item-scoped soft additive radial-core, tapered-streak and low-alpha dust/residue sprite textures, or use verified existing source textures only through cloned derived materials.

Muzzle: one compact white-hot radial core, one short warm-brass asymmetric wedge, one thin broken pressure arc that never forms a full bright torus, and 6-10 tapered micro-sparks confined mostly behind and beside the +Z origin. Overall length must stay compact and directional.

Flight: preserve the full body read; attach one restrained rear-seat wake approximately one-third to one-half body length using overlapping soft pale/brass sprites, 3-5 tapered kinetic streaks and sparse dark dust. No isolated straight needles and no wake in front of the body.

Impact: one compact white-hot contact sprite, one broken expanding fan/arc, 7-12 tapered sparks with visibly unequal length/width/brightness, and a short readable low-alpha smoke/dust residue. It must be compositionally distinct from Muzzle.
Use size-over-lifetime, color-over-lifetime and randomized rotation/velocity to remove uniformity while keeping a disciplined silhouette. Avoid giant blur, neon rods, full rings and visual noise.

Re-capture at more representative peak times if .032/.060 misses the volumetric core. Submit M peak plus a second near-peak frame, F hero/macro/gameplay/rear wake, I contact/peak/decay, clean termination frames and a baseline comparison before claiming readiness.
root_note: R3 is technically cleaner than R2 but remains below the user's minimum visual-quality floor. The dominant torus and hairline needles must be replaced by compact soft-core, tapered and volumetric particle compositions before another Root review.
